title: Reality Before Awareness
subtitle: Partial Views, Bounded Possibility, and Governed Agency
primary_question: How should an observer understand and act within a reality that can never be completely observed?
hypothesis: Partial awareness may be the normal condition of an observer embedded within reality. Reliable action therefore depends not on complete knowledge, but on bounded observation, declared uncertainty, proportional clarity, and governed agency.

principles.reality: Reality is not the same thing as awareness of reality.
principles.sufficiency: Awareness need not be complete. It must be sufficient for the consequence under consideration.
principles.alignment: Alignment must be evaluated within a declared envelope.
principles.clarity: Clarity is bounded and should remain proportional to available awareness.
principles.agency: Capability does not automatically establish permission.
principles.imagination: Imagination may exceed what has been observed without establishing external reality.
principles.simulation: A model may contain a reality without becoming the Reality containing the model.
principles.stewardship: Explore freely within. Intervene humbly without.

constraints: Partial awareness must not be mistaken for complete knowledge.
An imagined possibility does not establish external existence.
A model must not be confused with the system being modeled.
Uncertainty should be represented rather than hidden.
Different observational perspectives are not automatically incompatible.
Constructed assumptions should not cross into external consequence without sufficient evaluation.

observer_model.principle: The landscape need not change for awareness of it to change.
observer_model.interpretation: Changes in observational position expose different relationships within the same larger reality.

envelope_model.principle: Alignment is incomplete without a declared observational and consequential envelope.

R0.name: Containing Reality
R0.definition: The reality within which the observer, observation, model, and consequences exist.

R1.name: Observed Reality
R1.definition: The partial representation currently available to an observer.

R2.name: Constructed Possibility
R2.definition: Models, simulations, imagined worlds, and possibilities produced from or inspired by observed reality.

realm_flow.critical_error: R2 must not automatically be treated as equivalent to R0.

internal_storm.description: Human imagination can represent possibilities not required to correspond directly to external reality.
internal_storm.status: Real as mental representation without requiring the represented possibility to exist externally.

constructed_storm.description: Models, simulations, software, virtual environments, and artificial systems can externalize and manipulate imagined possibilities.
constructed_storm.purpose: Provide bounded environments in which alternate structures, assumptions, failures, and possibilities may be explored.

storm_model.boundary_principle: Freedom to explore a possibility does not automatically produce permission to impose that possibility on the containing world.

nature_model.principle: Incomplete awareness is not necessarily defective awareness.
nature_model.constraint: Natural systems operate within physical, ecological, relational, and consequential constraints without requiring human-style governance.
nature_model.distinction: Deliberate governance becomes relevant when capable agents can anticipate and intentionally produce consequences.

agency_model.governance_role: Governance bounds agency when consequences can extend beyond the exploratory or simulated envelope.

student_protocol.reflection_question: Did greater awareness change reality, or did it change the observer's relationship with reality?

failure_conditions: Mistaking partial awareness for complete knowledge.
Treating coherence as proof of truth.
Mistaking a model for the system being modeled.
Hiding uncertainty rather than representing it.
Treating different perspectives as automatically incompatible.
Allowing simulated assumptions to cross into external consequence without sufficient evaluation.

relationship_to_previous_leaf.previous: Modern Scams and Misalignments: Developing Resilience Through Awareness
relationship_to_previous_leaf.previous_principle: Do not grant more trust than the evidence supports.
relationship_to_previous_leaf.current_principle: Do not grant more certainty than awareness supports.
combined: Trust should be proportional to evidence.
Certainty should be proportional to awareness.
Agency should be proportional to both.
Governance should bound consequences when those assessments prove incomplete.

stewardship_protocol: Act proportionally to what is understood.
Govern consequences that extend beyond the boundary.
working_conclusion: Governance determines how responsibly those consequences may cross the boundary.
